title: Fold a paper crane
how: The one everyone starts with. About twenty folds, and the neck will probably come out a bit wonky the first time.
first_step: Cut a square from any printer paper and pull up a crane diagram.
moment_prompt: Your first crane, wonky neck and all.

title: Fold a jar of lucky stars
how: Each star is one thin strip of paper, folded and puffed up at the end. Very easy to do while something's on in the background.
first_step: Cut a few 1cm-wide strips from an old magazine page.
moment_prompt: The stars piling up in a jar or bowl.

title: Fold a box that actually holds things
how: A masu box needs one square sheet and no glue. Make one for keys, rings or loose change.
first_step: Find a square of thicker paper, like wrapping paper or an old calendar page.
moment_prompt: The box with something living in it.

title: Have a jumping frog race
how: Fold a frog each, press its back, see whose goes farthest. Silly in the best way.
first_step: Bring a few paper squares to coffee with a friend.

title: Hang a mobile in a window
how: Six to ten cranes or stars on thread, hung where the light catches them.
first_step: Fold one shape you like, then decide how many you can face making.
moment_prompt: The mobile up in the window.

title: Build a modular ball
how: You fold a dozen identical units, then slot them together. Fiddly for a while, then suddenly it's a sphere.
first_step: Fold 12 units from sticky notes before you try putting it together.
moment_prompt: The ball, or the pile of units so far.

title: Learn three knots with a shoelace
how: Lark's head, square knot, half hitch. That covers most beginner patterns. Practise before you buy any cord.
first_step: Tie a shoelace to the back of a chair and follow a short knot video.

title: Tie a plant hanger
how: The classic first project: square knots, a gathering knot, and a pot that floats in the air.
first_step: Cut about eight lengths of cotton cord, each roughly 4 metres long.
moment_prompt: Your plant in its new home.

title: Make a keyring to give away
how: Small, quick, and a good way to use up offcuts while you test a pattern.
first_step: Cut four 50cm lengths of cord or chunky yarn.

title: Knot a set of coasters with a friend
how: Pick one round coaster pattern and make four between you. They'll all come out slightly different, which is nice.
first_step: Split one roll of cord between you before you start.
moment_prompt: The four coasters side by side.

title: Hang it from a stick you found
how: Pick up a straight branch on a walk and build a wall hanging off it.
first_step: Find a stick roughly the width of your shoulders.
moment_prompt: The stick, now on your wall.

title: Swap leftover cord at a craft night
how: Macrame leaves a lot of offcuts. Trade colours with people at a library makers' group or craft meetup.
first_step: Bag up your leftovers by colour.

title: Stitch your initials on scrap fabric
how: Cross-stitch is just little Xs on a grid. Two letters is enough to know whether you like it.
first_step: Draw your initials on squared paper, one square per stitch.
moment_prompt: Your two letters, front and back.

title: Start a small beginner kit
how: Kits come with fabric, thread, needle and pattern, so there's nothing to work out before you begin.
first_step: Pick a design under 10cm across. Big ones take months.

title: Turn a photo into a pattern
how: Your cat, a plant, your front door, turned into little squares of colour.
first_step: Choose a photo with simple shapes and strong colours, then grid it on squared paper.

title: Stitch a tiny gift
how: A 3cm heart, leaf or initial on a bookmark or card. Done in a couple of evenings.
first_step: Pick one simple shape that means something to them.
moment_prompt: The gift, right before you hand it over.

title: Host a stitch night
how: Everyone brings whatever they're working on. Mostly talking, some stitching, plenty of tea.
first_step: Invite two people who have a project on the go, even if it isn't cross-stitch.

title: Stitch something cheeky
how: Sweet flowers around a blunt little phrase. It's a whole genre and very fun to make.
first_step: Write the phrase first, then sketch a flower border around it.
moment_prompt: The finished piece (blur it if you need to).

title: Hand-sew a nine-patch block
how: Nine squares in three rows. It's the building block of most quilts.
first_step: Cut nine 10cm squares from old shirts.

title: Lay out a memory quilt
how: Spread out the old t-shirts you can't throw away and work out where each one goes.
first_step: Pull every one of those shirts out of the drawer.

title: Quilt a pot holder
how: Small enough to finish in one sitting, and you'll use it the next day.
first_step: Cut two 20cm squares, plus an old towel for the middle.
moment_prompt: The pot holder doing its job.

title: Make a cushion cover from four blocks
how: A finished, useful thing before you commit to a whole quilt.
first_step: Choose two or three fabrics you like next to each other.

title: Swap blocks with a friend
how: Each of you makes a few blocks in the same colours, then you swap. Both quilts end up with a bit of each other in them.
first_step: Agree on a colour palette and a block size.
moment_prompt: Your blocks and theirs side by side.

title: Join a quilting group
how: Quilting groups meet at libraries, community centres and fabric shops, and they adopt beginners fast.
first_step: Ask at a local fabric shop when people get together.
moment_prompt: What the group is working on.

title: Learn the thumb push cut
how: The safest, most controlled cut. Practise it on a scrap stick until it feels natural.
first_step: Watch a short whittling safety video, then try it on any dry stick.
moment_prompt: A stick covered in neat little cuts.

title: Collect wood on a walk
how: Fallen branches from birch, willow or fruit trees carve nicely. Only take what's already on the ground.
first_step: Bring a bag on your next walk.

title: Whittle a tiny bird
how: Small birds are a classic first project, and they forgive a lot of mistakes.
first_step: Get a small block of basswood or soft pine and a sharp folding knife.
moment_prompt: Your bird, however it turned out.

title: Rough out a spoon
how: Not a finished spoon yet, just the shape. You'll feel how the wood wants to move.
first_step: Find a fresh green branch about as thick as your thumb.
moment_prompt: The rough shape with shavings around it.

title: Carve a butter spreader
how: A flat paddle shape. Useful, and a good step up from sticks.
first_step: Draw the outline straight onto a piece of soft wood.

title: Whittle round a fire
how: Camping trip or back garden. Everyone carves something while you talk.
first_step: Bring spare sticks and a cut-resistant glove for anyone new.
moment_prompt: What everyone made by the end.

title: Learn the saddle stitch
how: Two needles, one thread. It's the stitch behind every good leather piece.
first_step: Practise on any scrap, punching the holes with a nail.

title: Make a card holder from offcuts
how: Two pieces of leather and a few stitches. Lots of shops sell bags of offcuts for very little.
first_step: Buy a bag of leather offcuts and some waxed thread.
moment_prompt: Your cards, in the thing you made.

title: Make a keyfob
how: One strip, one rivet or a few stitches. Done in under an hour.
first_step: Cut a strip about 2cm wide and 20cm long.

title: Bring something old back to life
how: Restitch a bag strap or rub conditioner into a pair of tired boots.
first_step: Find one leather thing at home that needs some love.

title: Make bookmarks with a friend
how: Simple strips with your initials stamped or burned in.
first_step: Cut a few strips and borrow a set of letter stamps.

title: Take a one-day workshop
how: Lots of studios run beginner days where you leave with a wallet or a small bag.
first_step: Search for a beginner leather workshop near you.
moment_prompt: What you made by the end of the day.

title: Draw your coffee cup
how: Five minutes, any pen. The point is to look properly, not to be good.
first_step: Set a timer for five minutes.

title: Draw the same object ten times
how: Your shoe, from ten angles. By the tenth you'll actually see it.
first_step: Put it on a table and turn it a little each time.

title: Draw the view from one window for a week
how: Same view, different weather, different mood.
first_step: Pick one window and one small notebook.

title: Sketch people at a café
how: People move, so you draw fast and loose: shoulders, hands, the tilt of a head.
first_step: Get a seat with a view and something to drink.
moment_prompt: A page of strangers, no faces needed.

title: Go on a sketch walk with a friend
how: Walk, stop when something looks good, draw for ten minutes, swap books.
first_step: Pick a route with a few benches on it.
moment_prompt: Your two sketchbooks side by side.

title: Try a drop-in life drawing class
how: Lots of towns have one. Nobody's checking how good you are.
first_step: Look up drop-in life drawing near you.
moment_prompt: The one sketch you're glad you kept.

title: Hunt for good painting stones
how: Smooth, flat and palm-sized is the dream. Beaches and riverbanks are best.
first_step: Take a bag and walk slowly along the water.

title: Paint a stone and leave it for a stranger
how: Paint something cheerful, write a kind word on the back, leave it in a park.
first_step: Wash a smooth stone and let it dry.
moment_prompt: Your stone where you left it.

title: Try dot mandalas
how: Patterns built from dots with the end of a pencil. Calm and very forgiving.
first_step: Get acrylic paint and a pencil with an eraser on the end.

title: Paint ladybirds together
how: Red, black dots, done. Easy and cheerful, especially with kids around.
first_step: Collect a handful of round pebbles.

title: Paint plant markers
how: Label herbs or pots with painted stones.
first_step: Pick one flat stone per plant.

title: Leave a story trail
how: Each stone is a character. Leave them in a line along a path for someone to find.
first_step: Plan five characters on paper first.

title: Make a flipbook from sticky notes
how: Draw a bouncing ball across twenty pages and flick it. It's the whole idea of animation in five minutes.
first_step: Grab a pad of sticky notes and a pen.

title: Make a stop-motion with your phone
how: Move something a little, take a photo, repeat. Free apps stitch the photos together.
first_step: Pick one object, like a mug, a toy or a piece of fruit.
moment_prompt: Your first few seconds of animation.

title: Animate your name
how: Make the letters bounce, grow or fall apart.
first_step: Write your name big on paper or in a free animation app.

title: Animate a walk cycle
how: The classic exercise. Hard to get right, and you learn loads from it.
first_step: Find a walk cycle reference and trace it over 12 frames.

title: Shoot a stop-motion with friends
how: One tiny story, everyone moves something. Building bricks, food or clay all work.
first_step: Agree on a story that's 10 seconds long.

title: Watch a behind-the-scenes video
how: Seeing how animators plan a shot changes how you watch everything.
first_step: Pick an animated film you love and find a making-of video.
moment_prompt: One thing you'd never noticed before.

title: Bake a no-knead loaf
how: Mix it before bed, bake it in the morning. Very hard to get wrong.
first_step: Mix flour, water, salt and a pinch of yeast, then cover the bowl.
moment_prompt: The loaf and the first slice.

title: Make flatbreads in a pan
how: No oven needed. From bag of flour to warm bread in about half an hour.
first_step: Mix flour, water, salt and a spoonful of yogurt or oil.

title: Knead by hand for ten minutes
how: You'll feel the dough change from sticky to smooth. Oddly calming, and a decent arm workout.
first_step: Set a timer and try not to add too much extra flour.

title: Turn stale bread into something good
how: Croutons, breadcrumbs or a bread pudding. Nothing goes in the bin.
first_step: Find the oldest bread in the kitchen.

title: Bake two loaves and give one away
how: Keep one, give one. People remember being handed warm bread.
first_step: Pick a recipe you've made at least once before.
moment_prompt: The loaf on its way to someone.

title: Bake a bread from somewhere else
how: Focaccia, naan, challah, pão de queijo, roti. Pick one you've never made.
first_step: Choose a bread from a place you'd love to visit.
moment_prompt: The bread and where it comes from.

title: Make paneer
how: Warm milk, a squeeze of lemon, strain it. Fresh cheese in under an hour.
first_step: Buy a litre of whole milk and a lemon.

title: Strain yogurt into labneh
how: Spoon yogurt into a cloth and leave it overnight. Thick, tangy and very easy.
first_step: Line a sieve with a clean tea towel and set it over a bowl.
moment_prompt: Labneh with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Make ricotta and eat it warm
how: Same idea as paneer, but softer. Eat it on toast straight away.
first_step: Get milk, a little cream and some lemon or vinegar.

title: Watch how a cheese you love is made
how: Short documentaries show how milk turns into hundreds of different cheeses.
first_step: Pick your favourite cheese and look up how it's made.

title: Host a cheese tasting
how: Everyone brings one cheese. Taste from mildest to strongest.
first_step: Ask three friends to bring a cheese they love.
moment_prompt: The board before anyone touched it.

title: Stretch your own mozzarella
how: Pulling hot curd is messy and great fun. You'll need rennet and citric acid.
first_step: Order rennet and citric acid from a home-brew or cheesemaking shop.

title: Cook from whatever's in the fridge
how: No shopping allowed. Make dinner from what's already there.
first_step: Open the fridge and pick three things that need using up.
moment_prompt: The dish, with the name you gave it.

title: Write down a family recipe
how: The one nobody ever wrote down. Ask, cook it with them, then write it properly.
first_step: Call the person who makes it best.

title: Start a recipe notebook
how: Any dish you make twice goes in. Over time it becomes your own cookbook.
first_step: Write down the first recipe you know by heart.

title: Make one dish three ways
how: Change one thing each time: the spice, the method, the texture.
first_step: Pick something simple, like eggs, rice or potatoes.
moment_prompt: All three versions side by side.

title: Have a one-ingredient cook-off
how: Everyone gets the same ingredient and makes something different with it.
first_step: Pick one ingredient anyone can buy, like lemons or chickpeas.

title: Cook a weeknight dish from another country
how: Find what home cooks actually make on a Tuesday, not the restaurant version.
first_step: Pick a country and search for its everyday dinners.
moment_prompt: The dish and where it's from.

title: Learn the tasting words
how: Acidity, body, sweetness. Start noticing them in the coffee you already drink.
first_step: Look up a coffee tasting wheel.

title: Roast green beans in a pan
how: Keep stirring and listen for the first crack. Open a window, it gets smoky.
first_step: Buy about 200g of green coffee beans from a roaster or online.

title: Roast in a hot-air popcorn maker
how: It roasts surprisingly evenly. Do it outside or by an open window.
first_step: Find an old hot-air popcorn machine.

title: Taste a light and dark roast side by side
how: Same beans, two roasts, brewed the same way. You'll be amazed how different they are.
first_step: Roast two small batches and stop one earlier.

title: Visit a roastery
how: Lots of roasters let you watch, and some run free public tastings called cuppings.
first_step: Ask a local roaster if and when they do cuppings.

title: Host a home cupping
how: Slurp coffee off spoons with friends and compare notes. Loud, a bit silly, very educational.
first_step: Brew two or three coffees exactly the same way.

title: Shadow skip without a rope
how: Same bounce, no gear, no excuses. Good for learning the rhythm.
first_step: Bounce lightly on the balls of your feet for one minute.

title: Skip for one minute straight
how: Harder than it sounds. Count your misses and beat it tomorrow.
first_step: Find a rope and a patch of flat ground.

title: Skip through three songs
how: Song-length rounds with a short rest between each.
first_step: Make a playlist of three upbeat songs.

title: Learn the criss-cross
how: Cross your arms on the down swing. Feels amazing the first time it lands.
first_step: Watch a short criss-cross tutorial and try it slowly.

title: Watch a competition final
how: Competition jump rope looks impossible. Great motivation.
first_step: Look up a world jump rope championship video.
moment_prompt: The trick you want to try.

title: Try double dutch
how: Two ropes, two people turning, one jumping in. Very hard and very fun.
first_step: Get three people and two long ropes together.
moment_prompt: The first time someone got in.

title: Find a public table
how: Lots of parks, libraries and campuses have free outdoor tables.
first_step: Search a map for "table tennis" or "ping pong" near you.

title: Practise serves against a wall
how: Push one end of a table against a wall and serve into it.
first_step: Take a paddle and a few balls to any table.

title: Play best of three with a friend
how: Games to 11, keep score honestly.
first_step: Borrow paddles and a few balls.

title: Play round the table
how: Everyone has a paddle and runs round the table after each hit. Chaotic and brilliant with a group.
first_step: Get at least four people round one table.

title: Go to a club beginners' night
how: Clubs pair you with someone at your level.
first_step: Look up a table tennis club and ask about beginner sessions.

title: Watch a pro match at half speed
how: Ignore the ball and watch the feet.
first_step: Find a recent final online.

title: Keep a rally going in the park
how: No net, no rules. Just see how long you can keep the shuttle up.
first_step: Grab a cheap set with two rackets and some shuttles.

title: Do a footwork drill at home
how: Move to six spots like the corners of a court. No shuttle needed.
first_step: Mark six spots in a room or garden.

title: Rent a court for an hour
how: Indoor courts are usually cheap to book by the hour.
first_step: Book a court at your local sports centre.

title: Practise the high serve
how: Aim for the back line again and again.
first_step: Take a few shuttles to a court or a big empty room.

title: Join a social session
how: Lots of clubs run drop-in nights where everyone gets mixed together.
first_step: Look up a club near you and check their drop-in times.

title: Watch slow-motion smashes
how: Badminton is the fastest racket sport there is. Slowed down, it's beautiful.
first_step: Look up a world championship final.
moment_prompt: One shot you want to learn.

title: Stand on it and roll
how: Find where your feet go, push off, roll. Ten minutes on smooth flat ground.
first_step: Find a quiet, flat car park or path.

title: Learn to stop before anything else
how: Foot brake first. It makes everything else less scary.
first_step: Roll slowly and drag your back foot lightly along the ground.

title: Practise the ollie on grass
how: Grass stops the board rolling, so you can focus on the pop.
first_step: Put your board on the grass and practise popping the tail.

title: Go to the skatepark early
how: Mornings are emptier and friendlier for beginners.
first_step: Find your nearest skatepark and go before the afternoon crowd.

title: Skate with a friend and film each other
how: You'll see what you're doing wrong straight away.
first_step: Take turns on one board if you need to.

title: Watch a classic skate video
how: Skate videos are their own art form. Watch one all the way through.
first_step: Look up a classic skate video from before you were skating.

title: Learn to fall safely
how: Bend your knees and fall forward onto your pads. Practising this makes everything less scary.
first_step: Put on wrist guards and practise kneeling down slowly.

title: Glide round a car park
how: Flat, smooth and empty. Practise standing up and rolling.
first_step: Find a quiet spot on a weekend morning.

title: Learn one skate dance move
how: Something simple, like a grapevine. Look up a skate dance tutorial.
first_step: Practise the one move for ten minutes.

title: Skate a waterside path
how: A smooth path, a view, and a long glide.
first_step: Find a paved path along a river, lake or seafront.

title: Go to a roller disco
how: Rinks run music nights with skate hire.
first_step: Look up your nearest rink's adult sessions.

title: Skate holding hands
how: Two wobbly beginners are steadier than one.
first_step: Pick a rink session or a smooth path together.

title: Take a different way home
how: Same destination, streets you've never walked.
first_step: Look at a map and pick a route you've never taken.

title: Walk for half an hour without your phone
how: Leave it at home and see how it feels. Most people find it strange for ten minutes, then lovely.
first_step: Put your phone in a drawer and go.
moment_prompt: How it felt, written down after.

title: Swap coffee for a walk
how: Conversation goes somewhere different when you're side by side.
first_step: Text a friend: "walk instead of coffee?"

title: Join a walking group
how: Lots of free groups meet weekly from libraries, parks and community centres.
first_step: Search for a walking group near you.

title: Walk to the highest point nearby
how: A hill, a bridge, a tall car park. Look back at where you live.
first_step: Find the nearest high point on a map.

title: Walk 10,000 steps in one go
how: That's about two hours. Pack water and a snack.
first_step: Plan a loop, or a one-way walk with a bus or train back.

title: Do a proper push-up
how: Wall or knees first if you need to. Work up from there.
first_step: Try ten push-ups against a wall.

title: Stretch for ten minutes
how: The part everyone skips. Your shoulders will thank you.
first_step: Pick three stretches and hold each for 30 seconds.

title: Hang from a bar for 30 seconds
how: Builds grip and shoulders. Any sturdy bar in a park or playground works.
first_step: Find a park with a pull-up bar.

title: Learn a frog stand
how: The first step towards a handstand: balance on your hands with your knees resting on your elbows.
first_step: Practise on a soft surface for five minutes.

title: Do a full beginner routine
how: Push-ups, squats, rows and a plank. Three rounds.
first_step: Look up a beginner bodyweight routine and follow it once.

title: Train at an outdoor gym with a friend
how: Lots of parks have free bars and benches. You'll push each other.
first_step: Find an outdoor fitness area near you.
moment_prompt: The two of you at the bars.

title: Learn a basic step in the kitchen
how: Eight counts, slowly. Salsa, swing, bachata, whatever you fancy.
first_step: Watch a short basic step video and follow along.

title: Go to a beginner class on your own
how: Most classes rotate partners, so coming alone is completely normal.
first_step: Look up a beginner class happening this week.

title: Go to a social and just watch
how: Socials are where people dance for fun after class. Watching is allowed.
first_step: Find a social that starts right after a beginner lesson.

title: Practise with a friend in the living room
how: Lead, follow, swap, laugh a lot.
first_step: Push the coffee table out of the way.

title: Ask a relative to teach you a dance
how: Most families have one dance that comes out at weddings. Learn it properly.
first_step: Call the person who always dances first.

title: Dance at a free outdoor event
how: Warm months bring free dancing in squares and parks in lots of places.
first_step: Look up outdoor dance events this month.

title: Throw one ball properly
how: Hand to hand in an arc at about eye level. Everything else builds on this.
first_step: Roll up three pairs of socks.

title: Make your own juggling balls
how: Balloons filled with rice. Cheap and the perfect weight.
first_step: Fill a balloon with rice, then stretch two more over it.

title: Work up to a three-ball cascade
how: The classic pattern. Most people get it after a few days of five-minute sessions.
first_step: Practise for five minutes a day.

title: Juggle in the park
how: Practise outside. Someone will probably ask you to teach them.
first_step: Take your balls to a park.

title: Pass with a friend
how: Throwing to each other is a whole new skill and very fun.
first_step: Stand facing each other and practise one pass at a time.

title: Go to a juggling club
how: Lots of towns have a free weekly meetup, and they love teaching.
first_step: Look up a juggling club near you.

title: Spot the Moon in daylight
how: It's up during the day more often than you'd think. A nice way to start looking up.
first_step: Check a moon phase app to see when it rises.

title: Find five constellations
how: A free sky map app shows you what's what.
first_step: Go outside after dark and let your eyes adjust for 15 minutes.

title: See a planet's moons with binoculars
how: Even basic binoculars show Jupiter's moons as tiny dots in a line.
first_step: Check whether Jupiter is up tonight.

title: Watch a meteor shower
how: Several happen every year. Lie back on a blanket and look up.
first_step: Check when the next big shower is.

title: Go to a public stargazing night
how: Astronomy clubs and observatories put out telescopes for anyone who turns up.
first_step: Look up an astronomy club near you.
moment_prompt: What you saw through the telescope.

title: Get away from the city lights
how: Even an hour from town, the sky looks completely different.
first_step: Check a dark sky map for the nearest dark spot.

title: Eat lunch outside
how: Take your lunch to a bench instead of your desk. It counts.
first_step: Pack lunch and find a patch of grass or a bench.

title: Have an indoor picnic
how: Rainy day? Blanket on the floor, food on plates, no table allowed.
first_step: Spread a blanket on the living room floor.

title: Make everything from scratch
how: Sandwiches, a salad, a jug of something cold. Proper effort.
first_step: Plan three things you can make the night before.

title: Organise a bring-one-thing picnic
how: Everyone brings one dish. You bring the blanket and a game.
first_step: Send a message with a time and a park.

title: Have a sunrise picnic
how: Coffee and something sweet while the sun comes up.
first_step: Check sunrise time and pack the night before.

title: Picnic in a park you've never been to
how: Pick a green space on the map you know nothing about.
first_step: Find an unfamiliar park within reach.

title: Make a kite from a bin bag
how: Two sticks, a bin bag and some string. It really flies.
first_step: Look up a simple sled kite template.

title: Fly a cheap kite
how: All you need is wind and open space.
first_step: Buy a simple diamond kite.

title: Decorate a kite together
how: Paint or draw on a plain kite, then go and fly it.
first_step: Get a plain kite and some markers.

title: Fly at the coast
how: Sea wind is steadier and stronger.
first_step: Check the wind forecast before you go.

title: Go to a kite festival
how: Enormous, wild kites. Lots of countries have them.
first_step: Look up kite festivals this season.

title: Learn a two-line stunt kite
how: Stunt kites loop and dive. A completely different feeling.
first_step: Borrow or buy a beginner stunt kite.

title: Find your first cache
how: People hide little containers all over the world, and an app gives you the coordinates.
first_step: Download a geocaching app and pick an easy one nearby.

title: Swap a trinket
how: The rule is take something, leave something of equal or better value.
first_step: Put a small trinket in your pocket.

title: Read the oldest logbook you can find
how: Some caches have logs going back decades. Full of little stories.
first_step: Look for an old cache near you.

title: Find a cache somewhere new
how: Caches are everywhere, which makes travel more fun.
first_step: Open the app next time you're somewhere unfamiliar.

title: Do a cache trail with friends
how: Some trails link ten or more caches along one walk.
first_step: Pick a trail and plan a day.

title: Hide your own cache
how: Pick a good spot, hide a box, publish it for others to find.
first_step: Find a waterproof container and a small notebook.

title: Walk the tide line
how: Look along the line where the waves leave things behind.
first_step: Check tide times and go at low tide.

title: Look for sea glass
how: Old bottle glass worn smooth and frosted. Best in pebbly spots after a storm.
first_step: Walk slowly along the pebbles and look for colour.

title: Turn it into a scavenger hunt
how: Make a list and race to find everything.
first_step: Write down five things, like a feather, a crab shell, a round stone.

title: Pick up litter as you go
how: Take a bag and leave the beach cleaner than you found it.
first_step: Bring a bag and some gloves.

title: Identify what you found
how: Shells, seeds, egg cases, fossils. Look them up when you get home.
first_step: Take photos of anything you can't name.

title: Make a display of your finds
how: A tray, a shelf, a frame.
first_step: Rinse and dry everything you brought home.

title: Learn open vs closed
how: Closed jars make their own weather. Open ones suit succulents.
first_step: Look up which plants suit which kind.

title: Build a jar terrarium
how: Gravel, soil, moss, a small plant and a lid.
first_step: Find a clear jar with a wide mouth.

title: Collect moss on a walk
how: Take a little from walls and rocks, never too much from one spot.
first_step: Bring a small bag and a spoon on your next walk.

title: Add a tiny figure
how: A small animal or person turns a jar into a world.
first_step: Look in an old toy box for something tiny.

title: Make two with a friend
how: Share the soil and gravel and make one each.
first_step: Buy one bag of soil and one of gravel between you.

title: Go to a terrarium workshop
how: Plant shops often run evening workshops with everything provided.
first_step: Ask at a local plant shop.

title: Plant a tree seed
how: It'll take years. That's the point.
first_step: Plant a few tree seeds in a small pot.

title: Learn pruning basics
how: You shape a bonsai slowly, over seasons, one cut at a time.
first_step: Look up pruning basics for one common species.
moment_prompt: Your plan for the first cut.

title: Start from a nursery plant
how: Juniper, ficus and jade are forgiving for beginners.
first_step: Buy a small plant with an interesting trunk.

title: Share a tree with someone
how: A tree you look after together.
first_step: Agree who waters it on which days.

title: Visit a bonsai show or garden
how: Clubs hold shows with trees that are decades old.
first_step: Look up a bonsai club near you.

title: Repot into a shallow pot
how: A big step. Spring is usually the best time.
first_step: Find a shallow pot with drainage holes.

title: Arrange garden greenery
how: Leaves and branches look great on their own.
first_step: Cut a few stems from your garden, or ask a neighbour.

title: Rework a cheap bunch
how: Take a basic supermarket bunch apart and make it look expensive.
first_step: Buy one bunch and pull it apart on the table.

title: Try ikebana
how: The Japanese approach: a few stems, a lot of space.
first_step: Pick three stems and one simple vase.

title: Make a bouquet to give away
how: Wrap it in brown paper and tie it with string.
first_step: Pick a colour that suits the person.
moment_prompt: The bouquet before you hand it over.

title: Bring flowers for a friend's dinner table
how: Small and low so people can still see each other.
first_step: Ask what's on the menu and match the mood.

title: Go to a flower market early
how: Markets open early, and the best stems go first.
first_step: Find your nearest flower market and its opening time.

title: Play patience with a real deck
how: The original solitaire, no screen.
first_step: Shuffle and deal seven piles.

title: Learn a new two-player game
how: Rummy, spit, cribbage, gin. One deck, endless games.
first_step: Pick one and look up the rules.

title: Learn a game from your family
how: Every family has one. Ask the oldest person you know.
first_step: Ask a grandparent or older relative what they used to play.
moment_prompt: The game and who taught you.

title: Learn a proper shuffle
how: The riffle and the bridge. Satisfying and looks impressive.
first_step: Practise slowly for ten minutes.

title: Play in a café
how: Bring a deck and a friend and settle in.
first_step: Put a deck of cards in your bag.

title: Host a card night
how: Snacks, one deck, four people.
first_step: Invite three people and pick a game everyone can learn in five minutes.

title: Do a daily mini
how: Five minutes over breakfast.
first_step: Find a free daily mini crossword.

title: Solve one together
how: One reads the clues, one writes.
first_step: Print a puzzle or share a screen.

title: Learn how cryptic clues work
how: Every clue is a little riddle with its own rules. Once it clicks, you're hooked.
first_step: Read a beginner's guide to cryptic crosswords.

title: Make a crossword for a friend
how: A small 5x5 full of in-jokes.
first_step: Draw a 5x5 grid and pick five words.

title: Take one to a café
how: Paper, pen, coffee, nowhere to be.
first_step: Print a puzzle before you leave.

title: Join a puzzle group
how: Libraries and online groups solve together.
first_step: Ask at your library.

title: Solve a cube for the first time
how: The beginner method takes an afternoon to learn.
first_step: Get a cheap cube and follow a beginner tutorial.

title: Learn one algorithm a day
how: Small steps. Do it twenty times until your fingers know it.
first_step: Pick one algorithm and repeat it.

title: Time five solves
how: Use a free timer app and work out your average.
first_step: Do five solves in a row.

title: Race a friend
how: Same scramble, two cubes, who's faster?
first_step: Scramble both cubes the same way.

title: Teach someone to solve
how: Teaching it locks it in for you.
first_step: Find someone who has always wanted to.

title: Watch a cubing competition
how: Official competitions are held in lots of countries, and anyone can go and watch.
first_step: Look up competitions near you.

title: Learn the rules in ten minutes
how: The rules are simple. The game is not.
first_step: Try an interactive Go tutorial.

title: Play a 9x9 game against a beginner bot
how: Smaller board, faster games, nobody watching.
first_step: Download a free Go app.
moment_prompt: Your first game, win or lose.

title: Play a friend on paper
how: Draw a grid and use two different coloured pens.
first_step: Draw a 9x9 grid.

title: Watch a famous game with commentary
how: Some games are famous for one move.
first_step: Look up a famous professional game with commentary.

title: Visit a Go club
how: Clubs are usually delighted to see beginners.
first_step: Look up a Go club near you.

title: Get a real board and stones
how: The click of stones on wood is half the fun.
first_step: Look for a beginner set.

title: Learn the tiles
how: Suits, honours, flowers.
first_step: Look up a tile guide.

title: Find out which style people play near you
how: Rules vary a lot by country and family.
first_step: Ask friends or family which version they play.

title: Play an app first
how: Apps teach you as you go.
first_step: Download a free mahjong app.

title: Ask to join a family game
how: Lots of families have a regular game. Ask to sit in.
first_step: Ask an older relative if they play.

title: Host a mahjong night
how: Four players, one set, a lot of clacking.
first_step: Invite three friends and borrow a set if you need to.

title: Join a community game
how: Clubs and community centres often have regular tables.
first_step: Ask at a community centre.

title: Record five minutes on your phone
how: About anything you love.
first_step: Write three bullet points and hit record.

title: Listen like a producer
how: Pick an episode you like and note every time the topic shifts.
first_step: Write down the structure as you listen.

title: Interview a friend about their weird hobby
how: Everyone lights up when talking about the thing they love.
first_step: Write five questions.

title: Plan a three-episode series
how: Three is enough to know if you like it.
first_step: Write three episode titles.

title: Record on a walk
how: Walk-and-talk episodes have a lovely loose feel.
first_step: Take your phone out and talk as you walk.

title: Edit out the ums
how: A free editor, some music, and suddenly it sounds real.
first_step: Download a free audio editor.

title: Send your first postcard to a stranger
how: Postcrossing matches you with someone random in another country.
first_step: Sign up and get your first address.
moment_prompt: The card before you post it.

title: Make your own postcards
how: Draw, collage or print your photos onto card.
first_step: Cut thin card to postcard size.

title: Pick a card that shows where you live
how: Something that says your town.
first_step: Look in a local shop or make one.

title: Start together with a friend
how: Each send one and compare who writes back first.
first_step: Sign up together.

title: Put up the cards you receive
how: A wall of the world.
first_step: Pick a wall or a pinboard.

title: Go to a postcard meetup
how: Postcrossers meet up to sign cards together.
first_step: Look up a meetup near you.

title: Set up your first page
how: A key and a to-do list. Keep it ugly.
first_step: Grab any notebook and a pen.

title: Make a habit tracker
how: Days across, habits down, colour in a square when you do it.
first_step: Pick three habits.

title: Draw a monthly spread
how: A calendar, a few goals, a doodle.
first_step: Draw a simple grid for the month.

title: Learn one lettering style
how: Headers that look good, one alphabet at a time.
first_step: Practise one alphabet slowly.

title: Plan pages with a friend
how: Sit together over tea, each working on your own notebook.
first_step: Invite a friend round.

title: Look back at last month
how: What worked, what didn't, what you'll change.
first_step: Read through last month's pages.

title: Read one short essay
how: Something under ten pages.
first_step: Look up a famous short essay.

title: Read a classic one page a day
how: Slow is fine. Slow is better.
first_step: Pick one short classic.

title: Write a one-page answer
how: Pick a question that bugs you and answer it yourself.
first_step: Choose the question.

title: Listen to a philosophy podcast on a walk
how: Good ideas land better when you're moving.
first_step: Find a beginner-friendly episode.
moment_prompt: One idea you kept thinking about.

title: Argue one big question with a friend
how: Is it ever fine to lie? Do we have free will? Walk while you talk.
first_step: Pick one question each.

title: Go to a philosophy café
how: Discussion groups meet in cafés, pubs and libraries.
first_step: Look up a philosophy discussion group near you.

title: Sing one song at home
how: Lyrics on screen, nobody listening.
first_step: Pick a song you know by heart.

title: Perfect one go-to song
how: Find something in your range and really learn it.
first_step: Pick a song that sits comfortably in your voice.

title: Sing a song in another language
how: A song you love in a language you don't speak.
first_step: Look up the lyrics with pronunciation.

title: Duet at home
how: Pick a classic duet and commit fully.
first_step: Choose the song together.

title: Book a private room with friends
how: Far less pressure than a bar stage.
first_step: Book a karaoke room for a few people.

title: Sing one song at a karaoke night
how: Sign up, sing one, sit down. You'll feel great.
first_step: Find a karaoke night near you.

title: Learn three chords
how: On guitar, ukulele or keyboard, three chords unlock hundreds of songs.
first_step: Borrow an instrument from a friend.

title: Play one song all the way through
how: Badly is fine. All the way through is the point.
first_step: Pick a song with only three or four chords.

title: Play a song with a friend
how: One plays, one sings.
first_step: Pick a song you both know.

title: Try something you've never touched
how: Music shops usually let you have a go.
first_step: Visit a music shop and ask.

title: Take one lesson
how: A teacher fixes bad habits before they set.
first_step: Book a trial lesson.

title: Go to an open jam
how: Bars and community spaces host jams where anyone can join.
first_step: Look up an open jam near you.

title: Learn the three basic sounds
how: Kick drum, hi-hat and snare. Start by saying "boots and cats" slowly.
first_step: Say "boots and cats" ten times.

title: Watch a beatbox battle
how: The skill level is wild.
first_step: Look up a beatbox championship final.
moment_prompt: The sound you want to learn.

title: Layer a loop on your phone
how: A free loop app turns you into a one-person band.
first_step: Download a free loop app.

title: Practise on a walk
how: Work on one sound, quietly, as you walk.
first_step: Pick one sound for today.

title: Make a beat with a friend
how: One does the bass, one does the drums.
first_step: Agree on a tempo.

title: Go to a beatbox meetup
how: Communities meet in lots of cities, and they're very welcoming.
first_step: Look up a meetup near you.

title: Cut 30 seconds from your week
how: Five clips, one song.
first_step: Pick five clips from your camera roll.

title: Learn J and L cuts
how: When the sound leads the picture or lingers after it. It's what makes edits feel smooth.
first_step: Watch a short tutorial and try one.

title: Recut a film trailer
how: Turn a comedy into a horror.
first_step: Pick a trailer and a free editor.

title: Edit a trip into two minutes
how: Your best twenty clips, cut down hard.
first_step: Pick your twenty best clips.

title: Film one second every hour
how: A whole day in a few seconds.
first_step: Set an hourly reminder.

title: Shoot and edit a day with a friend
how: Pick a theme, film all day, edit together that evening.
first_step: Choose a theme.

title: Save stamps from your post
how: Soak them off the envelope in warm water.
first_step: Soak one stamp and dry it flat between paper.

title: Pick a theme
how: Birds, boats, space, one country. A theme makes it a collection.
first_step: Choose one theme.

title: Look up one stamp's story
how: Every stamp was printed for a reason.
first_step: Pick an old stamp and search for it.

title: Mount your first page
how: Arrange a page in an album.
first_step: Get a cheap album and some hinges.

title: Swap with a friend abroad
how: Send each other envelopes with interesting stamps.
first_step: Write to someone who lives in another country.

title: Go to a stamp fair
how: Dealers sell cheap starter bags full of stamps.
first_step: Look up a stamp fair or club meeting.

title: Learn the opening movement
how: Slow, calm, just breath and arms.
first_step: Follow a beginner video.

title: Do ten minutes before bed
how: The same short routine every night.
first_step: Pick one routine and stick to it for a week.

title: Practise outside at sunrise
how: Quiet, cool, lovely.
first_step: Set an alarm for sunrise.

title: Mirror a friend
how: Face each other and follow the same video.
first_step: Pick a beginner video.

title: Join a morning group in the park
how: Groups practise outdoors in lots of cities. Newcomers just stand at the back.
first_step: Ask around or look for a morning group near you.

title: Take a class
how: A teacher spots the tiny things you can't see yourself.
first_step: Find a beginner class.

title: Stretch at your desk
how: Neck, shoulders, wrists. Five minutes.
first_step: Set a reminder for mid-afternoon.

title: Do a morning routine
how: Five stretches to wake your body up.
first_step: Pick five stretches and do them before coffee.

title: Work towards touching your toes
how: Track it over a few weeks.
first_step: Measure how far you can reach today.

title: Stretch in the park after a walk
how: Fresh air helps.
first_step: Stop at a bench on your way back.

title: Try partner stretches
how: Some stretches work better with someone gently helping.
first_step: Find a partner stretching video.

title: Join a mobility class
how: Gyms and studios run them for all levels.
first_step: Look up a class near you.

title: Alter something you own
how: Hem some trousers or take in a shirt.
first_step: Pick one thing that doesn't quite fit.

title: Sew a tote bag
how: Straight lines only. You'll use it forever.
first_step: Cut two rectangles of fabric.

title: Find fabric second-hand
how: Old sheets, curtains and tablecloths are cheap fabric.
first_step: Visit a charity or second-hand shop.

title: Make elastic-waist shorts
how: A great first garment.
first_step: Find a free beginner pattern.

title: Sew alongside a friend
how: Share a machine, share tips, one project each.
first_step: Plan one simple project each.

title: Go to a sewing café
how: Rent machine time and get help when you're stuck.
first_step: Look up a sewing café or makerspace near you.

title: Explore a collection online
how: Lots of museums put their whole collection online.
first_step: Pick a museum's website and wander.

title: Spend an hour in one room
how: Skip the rest. Really look at one room.
first_step: Pick a room when you arrive.

title: Go on a free day
how: Many museums have free days or free hours.
first_step: Check when your nearest museum is free.

title: Each pick a favourite
how: Split up, then meet and explain your pick.
first_step: Pick a museum and a meeting point.

title: Go to a late opening
how: Museums at night feel completely different.
first_step: Look up late openings this month.

title: Visit a tiny odd museum
how: Small, strange museums are often the best ones.
first_step: Search for small museums near you.

title: Sit in a café for an hour
how: Notice, don't stare.
first_step: Get a window seat.
moment_prompt: One thing you noticed (no photos of strangers).

title: Write tiny stories about strangers
how: Imagine where they're going and why.
first_step: Bring a small notebook.

title: Sit near arrivals at a station
how: Reunions and goodbyes all day long.
first_step: Find a seat near the arrivals area.

title: Play the guessing game
how: Guess what people do for a living. No way to check, which is the fun.
first_step: Pick a bench with a friend.

title: Do quick gesture sketches
how: Thirty seconds per person, no faces needed.
first_step: Bring a pencil and paper.

title: Watch a neighbourhood you don't know
how: A different part of town, a different rhythm.
first_step: Pick an area on the map you've never been to.

title: Write five jokes
how: Start with something that annoyed you this week.
first_step: Write down one thing that annoyed you.

title: Record yourself telling a story
how: Watch it back and cut the boring bits.
first_step: Hit record on your phone and tell one true story.

title: Test a joke on a friend
how: Tell it over dinner and see what lands.
first_step: Pick three jokes to try.

title: Watch an open mic
how: Watch first, sign up another time.
first_step: Find an open mic night near you.

title: Do five minutes at an open mic
how: Terrifying and great.
first_step: Sign up and run your set out loud three times.

title: Take a beginner comedy or improv class
how: Lots of places run short courses.
first_step: Look up a beginner class near you.
